chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd, from 'Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
'Verily, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed zakat just as He imposed salat; and if a man were to carry the zakat and give it openly, there would be no fault upon him for that.

And that is because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, imposed in the wealth of the rich, for the poor, what would suffice the poor; and had He known that what He imposed for them would not suffice them, He would have increased it for them. And rather, the poor come into what they experience due to the withholding of those who withhold their rights from them — not due to the prescribed rate.'

key_terms.الزَّكَاةَ: Zakat — the obligatory alms-tax prescribed in Islamic law, one of the five pillars of Islam. Here equated in divine authority with salat.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ: Salat — the ritual prayer, the central act of worship in Islam, used here as a benchmark for the binding nature of zakat.
key_terms.الْفَرِيضَةِ: Al-farida — the prescribed (rate or obligation); the divinely mandated amount, distinguished here from the practical shortfall caused by human non-compliance.
key_terms.حُقُوقَهُمْ: Huquqahum — their rights; the entitlement of the poor within the wealth of the rich, framed as a right (haqq) rather than charity.

ai.seo_question: Why are the poor still destitute if zakat is sufficient according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes that zakat is a divine obligation of equal standing to salat, and that giving it openly carries no social stigma. Crucially, the Imam asserts that the divinely set rate of zakat is inherently sufficient for the poor — if it were not, God would have set it higher. The cause of poverty is not an insufficient rate of zakat, but the failure of the wealthy to fulfill their obligations.
word_analysis: He would have increased for them

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Al Husayn Bin Saeed, from Al Nazar Bin Suweyd, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Imposed the Zakāt just as Heazwj Imposed the Salāt; and if a man were to carry the Zakāt and give it publicly, there would not be a fault upon him,

and that is because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic Imposed in the wealth of the rich for the poor, what the poor would be sufficing with, and had Heazwj Known, that what Heazwj has Imposed for them would not suffice them. Heazwj would Have Increased it for them, and rather the poor are coming into what they are in (poverty), it is due to the prevention of the one who prevents their rights from them, and not from the (rate of Zakāt) Imposed’.
en.sarwar: 7. A number of our people have narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Husayn ibn Sa‘id from al-Nadr ibn al-Suwayd from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that
Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has made paying zakat compulsory as He has made performing of Salah (prayer) obligatory. If a man pays zakat publicly, it is not a blamable thing to do.

It is because Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Glorious, has assigned a share in the properties of affluent people for the needy enough to meet their needs. If it were in His knowledge that such share is not enough for them, He would have increased it. What the needy people face is because of withholding payment of zakat which is denying the rights of the needy, not because of the degree of the amount made compulsory.”
